articles.title: Alex Pereira Has a BIG Problem #ufc
articles.description: Did Ciryl Gane expose a weakness in Alex Pereira that could become an even bigger problem against Sergei Pavlovich? Chael Sonnen isn't convinced Pereira simply lost because Gane was bigger. After watching the fight, Chael points to something else: Gane's unusually aggressive forward pressure and the way he forced Pereira to fight on the back foot. Chael has seen Pereira train up close and remains impressed by his ability. But this raises a serious question: **Does Pereira struggle when a powerful striker relentlessly comes forward?** Gane didn't just rely on his size, Chael argues. He may have been the better kickboxer that night. And if that's the real explanation, Pereira has a specific problem to address. But if the size difference was the deciding factor, the challenge against Sergei Pavlovich could be even more concerning. Pavlovich brings heavyweight power and a dangerous striking game of his own. So what did Pereira's loss actually reveal — a technical weakness, a size disadvantage, or both? Chael breaks down the matchup and explains why the answer could determine Pereira's future against heavyweight contenders. #ChaelSonnen #AlexPereira #CirylGane #SergeiPavlovich #UFC #MMA #UFCHeavyweight #MMAAnalysis

articles.title: Joshua Kept the Fight in the UK. Big Deal!
articles.description: Anthony Joshua is getting praised as a man of the people for keeping the Tyson Fury fight in the UK. Chael Sonnen is not buying it, and he says Tyson Fury, the guy willing to fight anywhere to make it happen, is the one who got this right. Chael's test is simple: if you do the fight for the people, the people should not be the ones paying for the gesture. Everyone can watch this fight from anywhere and get the same result and the same resolution. Holding it in the UK just means UK fans pay far more to be there live. That is not serving the people, that is reaching in their pocket. Chael contrasts it with Kid Rock's small-venue tour: a hard $20 ticket cap, no promoter allowed to charge more, and 30 minutes of karaoke so fans could say they opened for Kid Rock. That is a man of the people, actions and a real loss, not words. Then Chael names the real story. Fury and Joshua are not fighting for anything, there is nothing on the line, and this fight does well only if nothing runs against it. The fight that matters is Eddie Hearn vs Dana White. Eddie said Dana cannot be on the stage. Chael says the ring is the ultimate stage: if Dana is in it on fight night, Dana wins. Now he wants Ariel Helwani to set the terms with him and accept them publicly. Who wins, Eddie Hearn or Dana White? Tell us in the comments, and subscribe for more from Chael every weekday. 0:00 Keeping the Fury fight in the UK: big deal? 0:36 Man of the people? Then why do the people pay? 1:16 Kid Rock did it right: $20 tickets, fan karaoke openers 2:43 What did Joshua actually do for the UK? 4:24 There has to be a winner and a loser: Hearn vs White 4:47 Eddie said Dana cannot be on the stage 5:08 The ring is the ultimate stage: if Dana is in it, Dana wins 6:11 Fury vs Joshua is not what you think 6:50 This fight will not sell out at these prices 7:26 The real story is Eddie and Dana 8:05 The challenge to Ariel: name your terms #UFC #Boxing #ChaelSonnen #FuryJoshua #DanaWhite

articles.title: Jon Jones Revealed His Biggest Regret
articles.description: Jon Jones says the biggest regret of his life, not just his career, is not being at the White House. Chael Sonnen was surprised Jones has any regrets at all, and he breaks down what Jones actually meant. The rumor at the time was Jones vs Ciryl Gane for an interim title in the absence of Tom Aspinall, if not an undisputed fight with the belt pulled from Aspinall to make history. Chael also reads the regret another way: Jones may mean not taking the Alex Pereira fight on that stage. Jones called beating Stipe Miocic at Madison Square Garden his greatest moment, one he does not believe he can redo. He also says he does not know if he will fight again, but he stayed in the testing pool, and Chael explains why that one detail says everything. Then Chael gets into how Jones actually works. Jones measures greatness by hardware and title defenses, not skill, the same belief he carried into the Stipe fight. And to produce the meanest, nastiest version of himself anyone has ever seen that night, Jones convinced himself Stipe had talked about his children. Stipe never said it. Chael compares that night to Mike Tyson's 93 seconds against Michael Spinks: for one night, that one version, nobody beats him. Jones will not come back for accomplishment, he already gave a belt back at light heavyweight, and money has never motivated him either. If he fights again, Chael says there is only one way it happens: a direct, public, personal insult, and there is only one man under contract who can deliver it. What do you think it would take to bring Jon Jones back? Tell us in the comments, and subscribe for more from Chael every weekday. 0:00 Jon Jones: not being at the White House is his biggest regret 0:24 The rumor: Jones vs Gane for an interim title 0:53 Or was the regret not taking Alex Pereira? 1:53 Stipe at MSG was his greatest moment 2:27 He may never fight again, but he stayed in the testing pool 3:14 How Jones measures greatness: Tito Ortiz and title defenses 4:39 Hardware over skill: the Jordan vs LeBron argument 5:32 Jones has to get dark: the insult Stipe never made 6:11 The nastiest version of Jon Jones anyone ever faced 6:54 Tyson's 93 seconds vs Spinks, and Jones vs Stipe 8:16 Not accomplishment, not money: what won't bring him back 9:38 Still in the pool for a reason: motivation, not the opponent 10:10 Only one man under contract can get Jon angry #UFC #MMA #JonJones #ChaelSonnen #StipeMiocic

articles.title: A Henderson-Bisping Moment, Handled Differently
articles.description: Andre Fili had his opponent down and out, with one more shot available to him, well within the rules, in the exact spot Dan Henderson once made famous against Michael Bisping. At the last millisecond, Fili moved the punch to the side and never touched him. Chael Sonnen says that is sportsmanship, and his only complaint about the whole thing is the line Fili said afterward, because Chael wishes he had said it first. Chael is clear about Fili: this is a guy who is nice to nobody in that ring, down and dirty, willing to go wherever a fight goes. That is what makes the moment matter. The extra shot was legal, the referee had not pulled him off yet, and it was completely unnecessary. It would not have changed the outcome. It could only have hurt a man who was already beaten. From there, Chael lays out his whole code. You never try to make your opponent look bad. His old wrestling coach stopped matches for that one reason alone. And taking it easy on somebody is not respect either, not in kids football, and not when fans paid to see LeBron play. Bring your best, beat him decisively, and then be done. That is where it ends. Where do you land: pull the punch, or take the free shot? Tell us in the comments, and subscribe for more from Chael every weekday. articles.title: Khamzat to 205? My Answer Is No
articles.description: Khamzat Chimaev wants a second belt at 205 pounds, and Beneil Dariush just told him to go get it. Chael Sonnen says hold on, because the size story everyone is repeating about Chimaev is not true, and Chael has the scale to prove it. Chael takes apart the famous weight claims piece by piece. The report that Chimaev lost 42 pounds to fight Sean Strickland, in a week, then in three weeks, never happened in any version, and Chael does not believe Chimaev has ever weighed 220 pounds. His evidence: four weeks ago at a Real American Freestyle event, the weight class was 195, Tyron Woodley weighed more than Chimaev did, and Chimaev stepped on the scale at 193 pounds without cutting a thing, the smaller man against a career welterweight. This is a guy who became famous on Fight Island by fighting at 185 and making 170 six days later, and he trains twice a day, every day. None of that means he would lose at 205. Chael co-signs Dariush: Chimaev would be a problem there and would probably take the belt. The problem is what comes after. Win that belt and you stay at 205 for good, and telling a 193-pound man to live at 205 is not wise. Asked for a yes or no, Chael's answer is no. Should Chimaev chase the second belt or defend at 185? Tell us in the comments, and subscribe for more from Chael every weekday. articles.title: Why Don't You Like Brendan Allen?
articles.description: Brendan Allen just won his fourth straight fight, submitting Christian Leroy Duncan in the fifth round of a UFC main event, and his reward is the same as always: nobody is talking about him. Allen says it himself, the fans do not like him and he is not over. Chael Sonnen likes Brendan Allen, so why did even he ignore him? Chael breaks down how a winning middleweight with finishes on his record stays invisible: main event, no buzz, and an opponent who could not get him over. Then Allen did the one thing that changes the conversation. He called out the fight nobody else wants, former middleweight champion Dricus du Plessis, knowing exactly what he is getting into: a former champion and a hard night out. Is the Dricus callout the fight that finally gets Brendan Allen over, or is being unliked a problem no opponent can fix? Tell us in the comments, and subscribe for more from Chael every weekday. 00:00 Why does nobody like Brendan Allen? 00:44 Being unliked is costing him sponsors 01:08 The old thread: "Why is Brendan Allen so hated?" 01:59 Chael checks his own record: I never mentioned him once 02:52 I do like him, but liking him isn't helping him 03:28 Stuck on the hump: the main event gives him the final say 04:25 Getting over is opponent-based, and CLD wasn't that opponent 05:05 Taking his shot: he wants Dricus du Plessis 05:31 Dricus is in the most complicated spot in the UFC 06:30 Overthinking your lane hurts your career 07:00 Strickland's silence shakes up the division 07:51 Nobody calls out Dricus, except Brendan Allen 08:50 The verdict: Chael fully supports Allen vs Dricus #UFC #MMA #BrendanAllen #DricusDuPlessis #ChaelSonnen

articles.title: Jake Paul Just Put Sean Strickland on the Spot #ufc
articles.description: Was Jake Paul wrong to make his conversations with Sean Strickland public? Chael Sonnen thinks he may have made the smartest move possible. The discussion centers on Strickland potentially fighting Jake Paul and the complications of getting a deal done while Strickland remains under contract. Chael points to the money involved in Conor McGregor’s fights and questions why fighters like Strickland should accept a fraction of those earnings. He also explains why Jake needed to know whether Strickland was free to negotiate before moving forward. But here’s the key: Chael believes that if this fight is going to happen, making the situation public may be the only way to get it moving. Was Jake Paul out of line for revealing the conversations, or did he understand exactly how to put pressure on the situation? Chael breaks down the business, the money, and why a potential Jake Paul vs. Sean Strickland fight could be more complicated than it looks. #ChaelSonnen #JakePaul #SeanStrickland #MMA #UFC #Boxing #CombatSports #MMAAnalysis

articles.title: Does Gable Steveson Really Have a Glass Jaw? #ufc
articles.description: Does Gable Steveson have a glass jaw, or did he simply get caught by a devastating punch? Chael Sonnen pushes back against the criticism following Steveson’s shocking 12-second knockout, arguing that one moment shouldn’t define an athlete’s entire career. Chael explains why the circumstances matter. When an opponent is told repeatedly that he’s going to lose, that pressure can create a different kind of urgency when an opening finally appears. In this case, the punch landed by a trained professional fighter may have been enough to knock out almost anyone. And Chael points to Steveson’s debut, when he absorbed a massive elbow and impressed observers with his durability, as a reason not to jump to conclusions. The bottom line? A knockout this early raises questions, but it doesn't automatically prove a fighter has a weak chin. Before writing off Gable Steveson, Chael says fans should remember one thing: **it was only 12 seconds.** #ChaelSonnen #GableSteveson #MMA #UFC #MMAAnalysis #Knockout #Wrestling #CombatSports

articles.title: Can You Get a UFC Title Shot If No One Knows Your Name?
articles.description: New DraftKings Customers turn five bucks into one hundred and fifty in total bonuses, paid over 14 days. The Crown Is Yours! Most people will immediately tell him no. Chael Sonnen explains why that reaction may actually mean Duncan is doing exactly the right thing. The middleweight division is unusually unsettled. Khamzat Chimaev has talked about taking time away if the UFC doesn't book him soon, the championship picture remains unclear, and Nassourdine Imavov appears positioned to play a major role in whatever comes next. That creates opportunity. Chael explains why repeatedly associating your name with a title shot matters, even before fans believe you deserve one, and why Duncan could make an even smarter move if he beats Brendan Allen. Instead of asking for the belt, Chael believes CLD should grab the microphone and go directly after Imavov. A personal rivalry is harder to dismiss than another fighter simply asking for a championship opportunity. If Duncan plants that seed now and the middleweight division breaks the right way, he could suddenly find himself much closer to the title than anyone expected. articles.title: Why Strickland Won’t Walk Away #ufc
articles.description: Sean Strickland wants $1 million to fight Nassourdine Imavov — and Imavov reportedly came back with a $500,000 offer of his own, provided he beats Strickland. But Chael Sonnen doesn’t believe fear is what’s keeping this fight from happening. Chael explains why he thinks Strickland is still determined to reclaim the UFC middleweight title. After losing the belt, Strickland made it clear that he believed the championship had been taken from him. In Chael’s view, that motivation hasn’t disappeared. Strickland has already fought Imavov, so the usual accusations about being afraid of an opponent don’t carry much weight. The real question is what happens if the two sides can’t agree on the matchup. Does the UFC find a different opponent? Does the situation become more complicated? And how does the promotion handle a contender who still wants the belt but may not agree to the proposed terms? Chael breaks down the money, the motivation, and the difficult matchmaking decision facing the UFC. #ChaelSonnen #SeanStrickland #NassourdineImavov #UFC #MMA #UFCMiddleweight #UFCNews #MMAAnalysis

articles.title: Michael Bisping’s Pereira Claim Sparks a Bigger Question #ufc
articles.description: Could Alex Pereira be fighting for the final time? Chael Sonnen says he’s now considering something he never thought he would: Pereira losing to Sergei Pavlovich — and potentially walking away from MMA afterward. The conversation starts with Michael Bisping’s claim that Pereira’s flat-footed style could leave him vulnerable to a knockout against the heavyweight striker. Chael acknowledges the risk, but says the bigger question is what happens if Pereira actually loses. At 39, Pereira has already built an extraordinary MMA résumé. But Chael believes a knockout loss to Pavlovich could make the road back to another title opportunity much more complicated, particularly with a return to 205 pounds seemingly off the table. Chael has always believed in Pereira’s ability to win. Now, for the first time, he’s questioning what a devastating loss could mean for the former champion’s future. **Could Sergei Pavlovich deliver the knockout that changes everything for Alex Pereira?** #ChaelSonnen #AlexPereira #SergeiPavlovich #MichaelBisping #UFC #MMA #UFCHeavyweight #MMAAnalysis #UFCNews

articles.title: Chael To Shevchenko: 'What Happened? Tell Your Story'
articles.description: New DraftKings Customers turn five bucks into one hundred and fifty in total bonuses, paid over 14 days. The Crown Is Yours! Sign up using https://dkng.co/sonnen or through my promo code SONNEN. #DKPartner A week removed, and Chael still can't bring himself to call her the champion. She won the strawweight title, sure. But in his mind she didn't win the strawweight title, and she is not holding the UFC belt. He lays out why, and it starts with Valentina Shevchenko. Chael walks through the mystery that has him stuck: the word used was "vacated," which has a definition, it means she did it on purpose, like Khabib did. Except he never heard she was hurt. Never saw it on the great shows, never saw it in the threads, never saw a word on social media that she might not make the date. Then one day the vacant title is being fought for, and he's asking the questions nobody else will: was she in agreement with it? How long were these discussions going? Because if there is one thing more powerful in America than the doctor, the lawyer, the millionaire, or the producer, it is the victim. Is that what she is here? Along the way comes the most backhanded love letter he's ever given Shevchenko: the quietly unbreakable record, four title fights carried from the co-main slot, the mother who was a world champion, the sister who's a badass, the underground myth that she's a foreign spy because she's as good with weapons as without them. He hates how she tells that story. But he respects the hell out of the fighter. Chael Sonnen is produced by Bad Guy Inc. articles.description: New DraftKings Customers turn five bucks into one hundred and fifty in total bonuses, paid over 14 days. The Crown Is Yours! But underneath the headlines is a real story about Nassourdine Imavov, the number one contender who still has not been offered a fight in 2026. Chael lays out the Imavov situation from the inside. Imavov told him directly that he is not holding out and not waiting, he simply has not been offered anything. Strickland, for his part, wants more money for a rematch, which Chael calls completely natural. And when Strickland said publicly that the next fight should be Imavov's turn, not his, Chael calls it an honorable move in the mold of Alexander Volkanovski. The takeaway is Chael's prediction: Imavov's next fight will be for the world championship, likely against the winner of Strickland vs Chimaev. For a fighter in his prime, Chael argues, the wait will pay off. #ChaelSonnen #MMA #UFC

articles.title: Chael Reacts To Chris Hemsworth Hitting Thai Pads
articles.description: New DraftKings Customers turn five bucks into one hundred and fifty in total bonuses, paid over 14 days. The Crown Is Yours! Sign up using https://dkng.co/sonnen or through my promo code SONNEN. #DKPartner Chris Hemsworth is in Thailand hitting pads like he belongs there, and Chael is not okay with it. He wanted to roast the famous handsome rich guy, and he flat out could not do it. Chael breaks down the clip move by move: the one technical knock is Hemsworth not stepping off-line when he throws the rear leg kick, planting the foot and throwing, which Bas Rutten would tell you is the easiest opening in the book. He also calls it a cardio issue, not a skill issue, and gives the fix he gives everyone on pads: pull back the power to extend your rounds. Then comes the story that keeps Kevin James at the top of the celebrity pad-work list: the time Jason Lambert was supposed to be doubling James on camera, and Chael realized the entire brutal pad session was James himself. But Hemsworth is the first person Chael has ever seen who made him question that ranking. The challenge goes out to Mark Wahlberg: send the tape, let's compare.
